title: India Wins Two Golds and Four Silvers at International Mathematical Olympiad, Finishes Seventh Globally
excerpt: A six-member Indian team delivered the country's fourth consecutive top-10 finish at the world's most prestigious maths competition, held in Shanghai with a record 680 participants from 117 nations.
body:
• India secured 2 gold and 4 silver medals at the 67th International Mathematical Olympiad in Shanghai, finishing seventh globally with 166 points.
  • The result marks India's fourth consecutive top-10 finish at the IMO, competing against 680 participants from 117 nations in the largest edition ever held.
  • Gold medalists Aarav Gupta (Delhi) and Abel George Mathew (Karnataka) led the team, while Shreya Mundhada — who earlier won India's first-ever EGMO gold — added a silver.
  • India's STEM Olympiad season has been historic: the Chemistry team swept all four golds at IChO in Tashkent, a first, and the Biology team won one gold and three silvers at IBO in Lithuania.

India's six-member team delivered a commanding performance at the 67th International Mathematical Olympiad in Shanghai, claiming two gold and four silver medals to finish seventh in the global standings with 166 points. The result extends India's streak of top-10 finishes at the world's most prestigious mathematics competition to four consecutive years.

China's team swept all six gold medals to claim the top spot, followed by the United States with four golds. Russia, Singapore, Vietnam and South Korea rounded out the top six. India outperformed traditional mathematical powerhouses including Japan, the United Kingdom and France.

The Indian Medal Winners

Aarav Gupta from Delhi and Abel George Mathew from Karnataka won gold medals, placing among the top-performing individuals at the competition. The four silver medalists were Bairav Murugan (Karnataka), Kanav Talwar (Delhi), Sanjana Philo Chacko (Kerala) and Shreya Shantanu Mundhada (Mumbai).

Mundhada's silver adds to what has been a breakthrough year for the 17-year-old. In April, she became the first Indian ever to win a gold medal at the European Girls' Mathematical Olympiad in Bordeaux, France, where India secured its best-ever team ranking of sixth among 67 participating nations.

"In the last four years, the Indian Math Olympiad team has performed extraordinarily well. We have clinched a spot in the top 10 among 100-plus participating countries, which was not a very regular occurrence in the past."

— Prof. Prithwijit De, National Coordinator, Mathematical Olympiad, HBCSE

Record-Breaking Competition

The 67th IMO was the largest in the competition's history since its founding in 1959, with nearly 680 participants from 117 nations competing across two days of examinations. Each team of up to six pre-university students faced six problems spanning geometry, combinatorics, number theory and algebra, with a total of nine hours to solve them.

The Indian contingent was led by Anant Mudgal of Mathelots Pvt. Ltd. as team leader and Dr. Mainak Ghosh of the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE-TIFR) as deputy leader. Observers Siddharth Choppara of the Chennai Mathematical Institute and Adhitya Mangudy of MIT supported the delegation. Three of the mentors are former IMO medalists themselves.

A Historic STEM Olympiad Season

The IMO result caps an extraordinary run for Indian students at international science competitions in 2023. At the 58th International Chemistry Olympiad in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, India achieved its first-ever clean sweep, with all four team members — Debadatta Priyadarshi (Odisha), Harshit Singla (Punjab), Kabeer Chillar (Delhi) and Sandeep Kuchi (Hyderabad) — winning gold. The performance placed India joint-first globally among 93 competing nations.

At the 37th International Biology Olympiad in Vilnius, Lithuania, the Indian team won one gold and three silver medals. Bhavyaa Gunwal from Haryana took gold, while Soumil Maity (West Bengal), Nishit Kalani (Rajasthan) and Anmol Kumar (Punjab) earned silvers.

What It Means for India's Talent Pipeline

The sustained performances reflect years of investment in India's Olympiad training infrastructure, anchored by HBCSE-TIFR. Winners from these competitions typically pursue degrees in mathematics and computer science at leading institutions in India and abroad, according to Prof. De, building a pipeline that feeds directly into the global STEM workforce.

India's cumulative IMO record now stands at 23 gold, 76 silver, 80 bronze and 29 honourable mentions across 36 participations since the country first entered in 1989. The 2026 results suggest the upward trajectory is accelerating.
